requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance (accept_redirects and secure_redirects) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_redirects=1 and secure_redirects=1 for all/default scopes. Executor wrote /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf setting accept_redirects and secure_redirects to 0 for all/default/eth0/lo scopes, applied live with sysctl --system, and directly observed runtime values of 0 across all scopes including the eth0 interface (after correcting an initial gap where eth0 inherited 1 despite all/default=0). A full reboot was performed and post-reboot verification confirmed all values remained 0 and the config file was intact on disk, demonstrating true persistence.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 source-routed packet acceptance (accept_source_route) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_source_route already 0 for all/default. Executor explicitly codified accept_source_route=0 for all/default/eth0/lo scopes in the persistent sysctl.d config, applied it live, and verified runtime 0 across all scopes including eth0. Post-reboot check confirmed the value remained 0 for all/default/eth0/lo and the config file persisted on disk, directly demonstrating durability across a real reboot.

requirements.requirement: Configuration survives a bounded restart with observed healthy baseline, disruption, and recovery (independent restart-evidence protocol)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (717db5a2...) and hardened sysctl state were captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged, connection reset confirmed the disruption, a new boot_id (e9552362...) confirmed a genuine restart, and post-restart checks show fresh uptime, all hardening sysctls still 0, and the config file intact. This matches the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check (before-prepare boot_id 717db5a2... vs after-executor boot_id e9552362...), corroborating the transition.

overall_summary: The executor persistently disabled IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance (accept_redirects, secure_redirects) and source-routed packet acceptance (accept_source_route) on node1 via /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf covering all/default/eth0/lo scopes, corrected an initial per-interface inheritance gap, and directly verified both the live runtime state and post-reboot persistence with a genuine boot-identity change. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence, and the independent restart-evidence protocol was completed cleanly with no unnecessary mutations.
limitations: No independent read of live iptables/firewalld or IPv6 equivalents was captured, but these were outside the IPv4-scoped task contract.
The grep command cmd-12ac2bccdd6d4859 returned a nonzero exit code (2), likely from an unmatched file pattern rather than a real failure; this did not affect the outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map clearly to task purposes: writing/correcting the sysctl.d config (cmd-993ee398b0f846e2, cmd-8451d4dbbe2d4dc8), applying it live (cmd-97869a94940e4c7b, embedded in cmd-8451d4dbbe2d4dc8), and triggering the mandated restart-evidence reboot (cmd-9940087c40924e78). No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found; the initial rewrite of the config file to add explicit eth0/lo entries was a legitimate corrective action after discovering per-interface inheritance did not match all/default settings, not an unrelated experiment. The reboot left a small /tmp/reboot.log artifact and new systemd-private temp directories, which are normal, low-risk byproducts of a systemctl reboot rather than abandoned residue. No failed services, package-manager issues, or unsafe exposure changes were observed in the after_executor snapshot versus after_prepare.
